title: Fabric Spark Data Engineering Architecture
purpose: Show Spark entry points, managed pools, driver and executor execution, file-layout controls, and Delta output on OneLake.
accessibleSummary: Notebooks and Spark job definitions request managed Spark sessions. Capacity and pool configuration determine startup and resources. A driver schedules executor work with autoscale. Native execution can accelerate supported operators. Write optimization, V-Order, and compaction shape Delta files on OneLake.
longDescription: Interactive notebooks and production job definitions submit work to starter or custom pools. The pool creates a driver and executor topology within capacity constraints. The driver plans jobs; executors process partitions and can scale within configured bounds. Supported operators may run through the native engine while unsupported segments fall back to JVM Spark. Write-side controls manage file sizes and layout before Delta commits become available in OneLake.

nodes.detail: Starter pools favor quick defaults; custom pools expose size and scaling controls. Acquire prewarmed or on-demand nodes and personalize the environment.

nodes.summary: The driver builds jobs, stages, and tasks and coordinates executor work.
nodes.detail: The driver builds jobs, stages, and tasks and coordinates executor work. Optimize plans, construct stages, and schedule tasks.
nodes.whyItMatters: Task assignments and application state depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

inputs: Application code, logical plan, and cluster resources

drill.example: A shuffle splits an aggregation into dependent stages.

nodes.label: Executors and autoscale
nodes.summary: Worker executors process partitions while autoscale and dynamic allocation adjust resources.
nodes.detail: Worker executors process partitions while autoscale and dynamic allocation adjust resources. Execute tasks, shuffle data, and adjust executor count.
nodes.whyItMatters: Transformed partitions and task metrics depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Workers host executors; autoscale and dynamic allocation grow and release resources with demand.

inputs: Scheduled tasks, input partitions, and configured pool limits
processing: Execute tasks, shuffle data, and adjust executor count
drill.example: A wide join adds executors during peak stages then releases them.
controls: Min and max nodes, dynamic allocation, decommission
failureModes: Skew leaves one executor running long after others finish

nodes.label: Execution and file layout
nodes.summary: Native execution and write optimizations improve supported processing and Delta layout.
nodes.detail: Native execution and write optimizations improve supported processing and Delta layout. Route supported operators natively and apply selected write-layout controls.
nodes.whyItMatters: Computed rows organized for Delta files depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

evidence.note: Supported Spark operators can execute as vectorized native code; unsupported segments fall back to JVM.
V-Order reorganizes Parquet physical layout at write time for read-heavy workloads.

processing: Route supported operators natively and apply selected write-layout controls

drill.example: A read-heavy gold table uses V-Order; unsupported operators continue on JVM Spark.
controls: NEE setting, Optimized Write, V-Order, and compaction
failureModes: Enabling every optimization on a write-heavy workload adds cost without benefit

nodes.label: Delta on OneLake
nodes.summary: Spark writes engineered output into versioned Delta tables on OneLake.
nodes.detail: Spark writes engineered output into versioned Delta tables on OneLake. Write Parquet data files together with Delta transaction metadata.
nodes.whyItMatters: Versioned tables usable by Fabric engines depends on making this responsibility and its operating boundary explicit.

inputs: Computed rows, schema, partitioning, and write mode
processing: Write data files and atomically commit the Delta log
outputs: Versioned tables usable by Fabric engines
drill.example: A MERGE commits changed sales rows as a new Delta version.
controls: Write mode, schema evolution, partitioning, retention
failureModes: Small files and incompatible schema evolution degrade downstream reliability
